# The product vocabulary

The names of the FLUID commercial offering. This is the subset of the
vocabulary canon that applies to product repositories; it is generated,
and the authority is `tools/canon.py` in the canon repo.

## Approved names

| Name | What it is |
|---|---|
| **FLUID Fabric Ecosystem** | The whole platform. The diagram's full title is 'The FLUID Fabric Ecosystem'; every name below is a part of it. |
| **FLUID Spec** | The open contract specification at the centre of the platform. Two words, both capitalised. Never 'FLUID Specification'. |
| **Sovereignty Without Soil** | The positioning phrase for running sovereign workloads without owning the ground they run on. Title Case, because it is a named idea. |
| **Command Center / Command Centre** | The control plane: the web workbench where contracts, runs, catalogs and governance live. Two words, both capitalised. |
| **Business Simulation Lab** | The collaborative workshop environment inside the Command Center. Never 'Biz Lab', never bare 'Simulation Lab'. |
| **FLUX Simulation Engine** | The synthetic-data runtime. FLUX alone is the product name; the component is the FLUX Simulation Engine. Never 'FLUX Simulator'. Spec only today, so a present-tense capability claim is a finding. |
| **Outcome Optimiser / Outcome Optimizer** | Closes the loop between deployed data products and the business outcomes they were built to move. |
| **Data Product Factory** | The automated CI/CD pipeline around the Forge Engine. Never 'Data Product Studio'. |
| **Forge Engine** | The deterministic compiler from FLUID Spec to infrastructure. The CLI is `fluid`, the package is data-product-forge, the component is the Forge Engine. Never 'Forge Compiler' and never 'contract compiler' as a name — the verb ('one contract compiles to AWS') is fine. |
| **Computational Compliance** | Legal and security policy translated into executable code that runs with the data rather than beside it. |

## Retired — never write these

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| `\bFRINGE\b` | the sovereign edge (runtime) / the sovereignty tier / Command Centre self-hosted |
| `Agentics Transformation Pty Ltd` | Agentics Transformation Limited |

## Never brands — descriptive lowercase only

| Not a product | Write |
|---|---|
| FEDERATION | the federation registry (descriptive, lowercase) |
| FATHOM | the settlement engine (descriptive, lowercase) |
| FORGE (standalone, all-caps) | Forge Engine (the component) / `fluid` (the CLI) / data-product-forge (the package) |

## Licensing and provenance

Every file in this directory except `profile.py` is GENERATED or
VENDORED and is byte-identical in every repository that carries it.
That identity is the integrity guarantee: `check.py` hashes its own
source into `CANON_ID`, so a per-file edit — including adding a
per-repo licence header — makes the gate report BLIND. The same
bytes also ship into proprietary repositories, so no single
open-source header would be accurate everywhere.

The directory is therefore covered by the licence of the repository
it sits in, and is exempt from per-file header checks. `profile.py`
is hand-written per repo and is that repo's own file.

## Changing any of this

Edit `tools/canon.py` in the canon repo, run `python3 tools/canon.py
--self-test`, then `python3 tools/emit_product_guardrail.py --write`,
then `python3 tools/sync_guardrail.py --write <repos…>`. Editing the
vendored copy directly fails that repo's CI with a CANON_ID mismatch.
